clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: To compare groups (patients vs HC, FEP vs SCZ), the study used voxel-wise two-way ANOVA, Schreier-Ray-Hare tests on summary scores, and post-hoc Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U, and t-tests. To link deviations to clinical symptoms (PANSS scores), Spearman correlations were used with both voxel-wise cluster-based measures and whole-brain summary measures. To predict treatment response, ROC curve analysis was performed and compared using the DeLong test. Imaging-transcriptomics analysis (GSEA) was used to explore biological pathways.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling, after ComBat harmonization, effectively identified heterogeneous but significant patterns of dopaminergic alterations in psychosis patients, and striatal deviation scores predicted treatment response with accuracy comparable to standard methods.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study demonstrated that ComBat harmonization is effective for creating normative models from multi-scanner PET data. Patients with psychosis showed a ~3-fold increase in extreme deviations in [18F]FDOPA signal compared to controls, with heterogeneous spatial patterns (max 20% overlap). FEP patients showed more positive deviations, while chronic SCZ patients showed more negative deviations, particularly in cortical areas. Voxel-wise analyses identified significant group-by-dataset interactions in frontal and temporal lobes. While whole-brain deviation scores had poor predictive power for treatment response, striatal Z-scores replicated the performance of standard striatal Ki analysis (AUCs: 0.77-0.83). Correlations were found between deviation scores in frontal/temporal clusters and PANSS scores in an independent patient cohort.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Modeling is influenced by the choice of linear harmonization (ComBat) which may not capture non-linear site effects. Voxel-level analysis resulted in a high number of models failing to converge. The clinical sample was heterogeneous (SCZ, FEP, different diagnoses within FEP). The definition of treatment response varied across datasets. The sample size was still relatively small for a normative modeling study.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study successfully applied a normative model to an independent patient-only cohort (FDOPA_04) without matched controls, demonstrating the potential to reduce the need for acquiring HCs in future clinical studies. The framework also represents a step towards establishing quantitative PET imaging as a clinical tool, similar to DAT SPECT for Parkinson's disease.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study confirmed the necessity of data harmonization for multi-site PET studies, finding ComBat superior to smoothing. A key finding is the differential pattern of dopamine alterations at different disease stages: FEP patients showed more positive deviations (hyperdopaminergic state) while chronic SCZ patients showed more negative deviations (potentially indicating cortical decline). The study highlights the significant inter-individual heterogeneity in psychosis.
